title: PowerShell shellcode loader and full-access LSASS handles on SCRANTON/NASHUA
rationale: These findings share the same PowerShell session (PID 2976/3876) on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe with full-access masks (0x1f3fff, 0x1fffff) and query-limited 0x1000, plus wsmprovhost.exe on nashua.dmevals.local, preceded by accesschk.exe and a VirtualAlloc/CreateThread shellcode loader. LSASS memory access is best characterized as OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory.

title: DS-Replication-Get-Changes access on NEWYORK by machine account
rationale: A 4662 event shows DS-Replication-Get-Changes GUID access, the DCSync right, though by the host's own machine account on itself, so low confidence.

title: WebDAV forced-authentication from 10.0.1.4 to 192.168.0.4
rationale: DavClnt/WebDAV-MiniRedir OPTIONS/PROPFIND sequence with 401 then 207 shows the classic forced-authentication handshake to capture credentials.

title: Shortcut/lure file creation on SCRANTON
rationale: Explorer Recent .lnk files and a PowerShell-written StartUp hostui.lnk were created; the finding itself notes the StartUp .lnk is persistence rather than forced auth, but the lure-style shortcuts are best mapped to forced authentication among in-scope techniques.

title: Credential-harvesting PowerShell file collection on SCRANTON/NASHUA
rationale: Under pbeesly, PowerShell on scranton and nashua enumerated user profiles for *pass*/*login*/*vpn* and document files and compressed them (Compress-Archive, Rar.exe with password, sdelete64 wipe). This is harvesting credentials stored in files.

title: Invoke-Exfil staging and WebDAV exfiltration with embedded credentials
rationale: Both describe the Invoke-Exfil scriptblock (psversion.ps1) compressing Downloads into a password-protected 7z and copying to \\192.168.0.4\webdav with hardcoded cozy/MyCozyPassw0rd! credentials. The credential-access element is plaintext credentials embedded in scripts.

title: PsExec64 from SCRANTON passing cleartext domain password to NASHUA
rationale: PsExec64 invoked with -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by to launch python.exe on \\NASHUA, producing PSEXESVC logons. The credential-access aspect is a cleartext password in a command line.

title: Get-PrivateKeys certificate export to .pfx with hardcoded password on SCRANTON
rationale: Both findings describe the same Get-PrivateKeys scriptblock (readme.ps1) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and exporting certificates to .pfx with hardcoded password 'saribas', producing coyn5igj.3io.pfx. This is theft of private keys.

title: Unsigned hostui.exe launched elevated from PowerShell on SCRANTON
rationale: PowerShell ran Start-Process hostui.exe -verb runas; the unsigned, metadata-less binary at High integrity is consistent with a credential-theft helper accessing Windows Credential Manager.

title: No golden-ticket evidence despite LSASS access
rationale: LSASS access prerequisite present but no forged-TGT artifacts; mapped to Golden Ticket as the closest in-scope technique for the assessed hypothesis.

title: Hidden steganography-decoded PowerShell implant (monkey.png) launched via control.exe on SCRANTON
rationale: control.exe /name Microsoft.BackupAndRestoreCenter spawned hidden, execution-policy-bypassed PowerShell that decoded a payload from monkey.png and IEX'd it. This is obfuscated execution, not credential access.

title: Malicious .scr dropper in C:\ProgramData\victim executed by pbeesly on SCRANTON
rationale: Both findings describe the same event: explorer.exe launching C:\ProgramData\victim\<odd-name>cod.3aka3.scr with /S as pbeesly, spawning cmd.exe/conhost and later wiped with sdelete64. This is user execution of a malicious file, not credential access.
